business_model.claim: Talen Energy Corporation is a United States independent power producer that owns and operates approximately 13.1 GW of power infrastructure (including 2.2 GW of nuclear power) and sells electricity, capacity, and ancillary services into wholesale markets.
quotes: We own and operate approximately 13.1 GW of power infrastructure in the United States, including 2.2 GW of nuclear power and a significant dispatchable fossil fleet.
We produce and sell electricity, capacity, and ancillary services into wholesale U.S. power markets, with our generation fleet principally located in the Mid-Atlantic, Ohio, and Montana.

business_model.claim: Approximately 13 GW of Talen's generation capacity is located in PJM, where it sells capacity via Base Residual Auctions, Incremental Auctions, or bilateral transactions and sells energy and ancillary services into day-ahead, real-time, and bilateral markets.
quotes: Specifically, approximately 13 GW of our generation capacity is located in the MAAC (Mid-Atlantic Area Council), BGE (Baltimore Gas and Electric), and AEP (American Electric Power) regions of PJM.

We sell capacity through PJM Base Residual Auctions and, to the extent we are unable to sell capacity through the PJM BRAs, we may sell uncleared capacity through PJM Incremental Auctions or bilateral capacity transactions.
We sell energy/ancillary services into these markets.

business_model.claim: The remainder of Talen's generation capacity is at the Colstrip facility in Montana within WECC, where there are no centralized energy or capacity markets and Talen sells energy through direct bilateral transactions.
quotes: WECC does not operate energy or capacity markets.
We enter into bilateral transactions for the direct sale of energy from our portion of the generation from Colstrip.

quotes: At the full contract quantity, we will provide AWS with 1,920 MW of carbon-free nuclear power through 2042 (with options to further extend its duration) for operations at the AWS Data Campus adjacent to Susquehanna (with the ability to deliver to other sites throughout Pennsylvania).

The AWS PPA, which has minimum commitments, has a power delivery schedule that ramps up over time, which is expected to achieve the full volume no later than 2032, with the potential to meaningfully accelerate.
The AWS PPA requires Talen to deliver carbon-free power to AWS over a significant contract term at anticipated premium prices.

competitive_position.claim: Talen owns and operates approximately 13.1 GW of U.S. power infrastructure, anchored by over 5.7 GW of low- and zero-carbon baseload generation including a 90% interest in the 2.5 GW Susquehanna nuclear facility.
quotes: We own and operate approximately 13.1 GW of power infrastructure in the United States, including 2.2 GW of nuclear power and a significant dispatchable fossil fleet.

We own and operate over 5.7 GW of low- and zero-carbon baseload generation, including a 90% interest in, the 2.5 GW Susquehanna facility, the seventh largest nuclear-powered generation facility in the U.S.

competitive_position.claim: In 2025, Susquehanna produced approximately 17 TWh of zero-carbon power at a low all-in cost of approximately $27 per MWh.
quotes: In 2025, we produced approximately 17 TWh of reliable, zero-carbon power from Susquehanna at a low all-in cost of approximately $27 per MWh, while also maintaining excellent safety and operational performance (when measured by standards adopted by the nuclear industry).

competitive_position.claim: Talen expanded its natural gas fleet by adding 2.8 GW through Freedom and Guernsey in November 2025 and completing the Cornerstone Acquisition of approximately 2.5 GW in June 2026.
quotes: While Susquehanna has typically comprised approximately half of our total annual generation, we recently added an additional 2.8 GW of low-carbon generation—the equivalent of more than the entire Susquehanna plant—through our recent acquisitions of Freedom and Guernsey, which are some of the new newest, most highly-efficient H-class combined-cycle baseload natural gas facilities in the market.

In November 2025, the Company consummated the Freedom and Guernsey Acquisitions for an aggregate $3.8 billion which is subject to certain post-closing adjustments for net working capital and other customary items.

The addition of these assets to Talen’s portfolio will increase generation capacity by approximately 2.5 GW of natural gas generation, substantially expanding Talen’s presence in the western PJM market and adding additional efficient baseload generation assets to its fleet.

This is primarily related to higher generation facility operating costs due to: (i) an increase associated with the Freedom and Guernsey acquisitions and the Cornerstone Acquisition, which were completed in November 2025 and June 2026, respectively; and (ii) operations and routine maintenance projects at our dispatchable fossil generation facilities.

competitive_position.claim: Approximately 13 GW of Talen's generation capacity is located in PJM, with natural gas plants situated near the Marcellus and Utica shale regions of Pennsylvania and Ohio.
quotes: Specifically, approximately 13 GW of our generation capacity is located in the MAAC (Mid-Atlantic Area Council), BGE (Baltimore Gas and Electric), and AEP (American Electric Power) regions of PJM.

Further, our natural gas generation assets are situated near the Marcellus and Utica shale regions of Pennsylvania and Ohio, which provide access to fuel from some of the largest producing natural gas regions in the U.S.

competitive_position.claim: PJM summer peak load is forecasted to grow by approximately 66 GW by 2036, or 3.6% per year, while the PJM new-build queue is predominantly intermittent and coal retirements continue.
quotes: Summer peak load is forecasted to grow by approximately 66 GW by 2036, or an average of 3.6% per year over the next 10-year period.
This demand growth is not currently well matched with increases in supply, as the PJM queue for new-build generation is predominately intermittent rather than dispatchable in nature.

quotes: The AWS PPA requires Talen to deliver carbon-free power to AWS over a significant contract term at anticipated premium prices.

At the full contract quantity, we will provide AWS with 1,920 MW of carbon-free nuclear power through 2042 (with options to further extend its duration) for operations at the AWS Data Campus adjacent to Susquehanna (with the ability to deliver to other sites throughout Pennsylvania).

competitive_position.claim: Talen operates 2.0 GW of capacity at Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner under RMR agreements until May 31, 2029, earning annual fixed-cost payments of $145 million and $35 million plus variable cost reimbursement.

Wagner and Brandon Shores facilities, totaling 2.0 GW of capacity, under RMR agreements pursuant to which we receive fixed monthly payments in exchange for continuing to operate those facilities until May 31, 2029 (beyond their previously scheduled 2025 retirement dates) to maintain grid and transmission reliability in the Baltimore area until upgrades can be completed.

Wagner, which includes a performance “hold back” of $5 million per year for Brandon Shores and $2.5 million per year for H.A. Wagner, each to be paid out based on unit performance.

In July 2026, the Company cleared 10,180 MW in the PJM BRA for the 2028/2029 PJM Capacity Year at a price of $325.00/MWd.

competitive_position.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Talen generated 23.9 TWh at a 75.4% capacity factor and grew Adjusted EBITDA by $306 million year over year to $669 million.
quotes: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Talen reported GAAP Net Income (Loss) Attributable to Stockholders of $138 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $669 million, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $433 million.

Adjusted EBITDA increased by $306 million primarily due to the contribution of acquired generation facilities, higher settled power prices and generation volumes (net of realized hedges), and higher capacity revenues.

competitive_position.claim: Talen's first-lien hedging program limits margin posting requirements, while its nuclear fuel cycle is fully contracted through the 2028 fuel load and over 50% contracted through 2029.
quotes: Specifically, our hedging strategy prioritizes a first lien-based hedging program, in which hedging counterparties are granted a lien in the same collateral securing our first-lien debt obligations, while minimizing exchange-based hedging and the associated margin requirements.
Our nuclear fuel cycle is fully contracted through the 2028 fuel load, more than 50% contracted through 2029, and over 20% contracted through 2030.

competitive_position.claim: Talen lacks an assured regulated rate of return and competes in wholesale markets against rivals that may possess greater resources, newer facilities, lower costs, or more experience.
quotes: Our business model depends on us successfully operating in a competitive environment and, unlike regulated utilities, we are not assured of any rate of return on capital investments through a regulated rate structure.
Some of our competitors may have advantages over us through access to greater resources, newer generation facilities, lower costs, or more experience.

competitive_position.claim: Talen's competitive position faces threats from government subsidies favoring competing generation technologies, state re-regulation proposals, and changes to PJM market rules.
quotes: Competition may also be impacted by the actions of environmental and other governmental authorities, including but not limited to the establishment of legislation or subsidies favoring one form of generation over another (such as investment tax credits, production tax credits, and other factors); for example, the Inflation Reduction Act contains a number of tax credits and incentives relating to renewable energy projects and clean energy technologies.

PJM, the primary market in which we operate, is a competitive market and has from time-to-time considered new market rules, while some states have considered re-regulation measures that could result in more limited opportunities for competitive energy suppliers.

competitive_position.claim: Expected demand growth from data centers and manufacturing may not be sustained, and renewable penetration, energy efficiency, or generation oversupply could depress wholesale power prices and dispatchable unit economics.
quotes: A general economic slowdown or recession, a downturn in technology, manufacturing, or other sectors, an oversupply of generation resources or natural gas, or various other economic conditions could reduce electricity demand and prices.
Furthermore, the penetration of renewable generation resources has, and may continue to have, negative effects on wholesale power prices and the economics of dispatchable generation units.

competitive_position.claim: Because natural gas units often set marginal wholesale electricity prices, declines or volatility in natural gas prices can compress Talen's energy margins and revenues.
quotes: Because natural gas facilities often serve as the marginal, price-setting generating units, there is a strong positive correlation between the price of natural gas and the wholesale market price of electricity in the competitive power markets in which we operate.
A decline, or significant volatility, in the price of natural gas or other fuels could negatively impact energy margin and energy revenues.

competitive_position.claim: Unplanned outages or reduced output can cause lost margin, replacement power costs, PJM Capacity Performance penalties, and contractual remedies under the AWS PPA, even on monetized capacity.
quotes: Any unexpected failure, including those associated with breakdowns or forced outages, could result in reduced profitability, including from lost energy margin, costs to cover power at then-current market prices to satisfy our commitments, and additional repair and (or) ongoing maintenance costs.

Additionally, under the AWS PPA, we have committed to certain delivery quantities over time with agreed reliability standards and AWS may be entitled to contractual or other remedies in the event of our non-performance.

The Company remains responsible for operating its generation facilities, retains the obligation to perform as a PJM generation capacity resource with respect to the capacity sold in the transaction, has retained its rights for any earned capacity performance bonus payments, and has retained the risks associated with performance deficiency penalties.

competitive_position.claim: Because Susquehanna accounts for a substantial share of generation and earnings, nuclear operational disruptions, limited fuel component suppliers, and permanent spent fuel disposal uncertainty pose concentrated risks.
quotes: Because Susquehanna accounts for a substantial amount of our generation and associated earnings, any adverse development in Susquehanna’s operations, such as an unplanned outage or catastrophic event, could have a significant impact on our business.
In addition, the costs associated with the nuclear fuel cycle are substantial, and suppliers of certain components and other materials required to produce nuclear fuel are limited.

competitive_position.claim: Geographic concentration in the Mid-Atlantic and PJM exposes Talen to mild weather suppressing demand, regional disasters, and transmission congestion or outages that reduce realized plant prices.
quotes: Furthermore, as a significant portion of our power generation facilities are geographically concentrated in the mid-Atlantic area of the United States, we face increased risk that a natural or man-made disaster in that area could adversely affect a large part of our operations.

Furthermore, transmission constraints and outages, including line maintenance outages, can cause transmission congestion that negatively impacts energy prices at our facilities, which could affect the realized margins of our generation fleet.

competitive_position.claim: Extensive regulatory and environmental compliance costs, cyberattacks, hedging collateral demands during price swings, and counterparty credit defaults could constrain liquidity or curtail operations.
quotes: The costs of compliance with these requirements may be substantial, and any non-compliance or inability to comply could result in the suspension or curtailment of our electricity sales and power delivery; the cessation, suspension, delay, or limitation of our operations; premature unit retirements; and (or) monetary penalties, increased compliance obligations, or other types of sanctions.

The effectiveness of our commercial strategy may be dependent on the amount of collateral available to support our hedging arrangements, and these collateral requirements may be greater than we anticipate or are able to meet.

quotes: A decline, or significant volatility, in the price of natural gas or other fuels could negatively impact energy margin and energy revenues.

Our business model depends on us successfully operating in a competitive environment and, unlike regulated utilities, we are not assured of any rate of return on capital investments through a regulated rate structure.
Conversely, mild winter or summer temperatures in the Mid-Atlantic tend to suppress electric demand and may result in lower overall settled prices that reduce our energy margin.

risks.basis: stated in P2, P1, F1, and P3
risks.claim: Because Susquehanna accounts for a substantial share of generation and earnings, an extended or unplanned nuclear outage, fuel-cycle disruption, or unrecovered spent nuclear fuel storage costs could materially hurt earnings.
quotes: Because Susquehanna accounts for a substantial amount of our generation and associated earnings, any adverse development in Susquehanna’s operations, such as an unplanned outage or catastrophic event, could have a significant impact on our business.
Furthermore, there remains substantial uncertainty regarding the nuclear industry’s permanent disposal of SNF, which could result in substantial additional costs to us that cannot be predicted.

Consequently, the government is required to reimburse Susquehanna for certain SNF storage costs through 2025 under a related settlement agreement, which we are currently in the process of seeking to extend through 2028.

risks.basis: stated in P2, P1, and P3
risks.claim: Geographic concentration in the mid-Atlantic, third-party transmission congestion, and cyber-based security threats expose Talen to regional disruptions and lower realized energy margins.
quotes: Furthermore, as a significant portion of our power generation facilities are geographically concentrated in the mid-Atlantic area of the United States, we face increased risk that a natural or man-made disaster in that area could adversely affect a large part of our operations.

Furthermore, transmission constraints and outages, including line maintenance outages, can cause transmission congestion that negatively impacts energy prices at our facilities, which could affect the realized margins of our generation fleet.
We are also subject to cyber-based security disruption and integrity risk, which could result in an adverse impact to our results of operations or business reputation.
